reference.note: v0 = SO-101 URDF geometry + STS3215 on pan/lift/elbow/wrist_flex (wrist_flex user choice 2026-10-29, hardware-notes/2026-10-29-camera-teleop-arm-survey.md) + STS3032 on wrist_roll, gripper (user choice 2026-10-28, hardware-notes/2026-10-28-arm-4-1-component-review.md) + concept base. Replaced by v1 from the team CAD (FreeCAD) and v2 from measurements of the built arm.

sts3215_12v.accel_source: assumed: reach the speed cap in ~0.3 s; STS3215 register 41 (0-254 x 8.7 deg/s^2) can do it in the servo; tune in P009
sts3215_12v.source: Feetech C018 datasheet A/0 2023-07-20: 0.222 s/60deg at 12V, stall 30 kg.cm, rated 10 kg.cm

sts3032_6v.accel_source: assumed: reach the speed cap in ~0.3 s; STS acceleration register like STS3215; tune in P009
sts3032_6v.source: shop pages, not a Feetech datasheet (eckstein-shop.de, aifitlab.com): 0.09 s/60deg at 6V, stall 4.5 / rated 1.5 kg.cm at 6V, 20 g, 23.2 x 12.1 x 28.5 mm, 4096 steps/360deg; 6V rail, not the STS3215 12V bus power

joints.name: shoulder_pan
joints.limit_source: D25 base turns a full circle (+-180deg); URDF had +-110deg

joints.name: wrist_flex
joints.limit_source: URDF (+-95deg) inside STS3215 360deg travel; was MG996R +-79.5deg

joints.name: wrist_roll
joints.limit_source: URDF (-157..+163deg), inside STS3032 360deg travel; was MG996R -64..+95deg; cable twist through the roll not checked

joints.name: gripper
joints.limit_source: shell v1 gear crank in wrist_gripper_v1: 8.92deg = fingers touching, 60.17deg = 57 mm open; one servo drives two meshing gears and a parallel four-bar, so use gripper_kinematics, not this angle alone, for the finger position

soft_limits.note: Stricter than the joint limits; the adapter clamps targets to these. From cad/shell_v1 checks and docs/research/hardware-notes/2026-10-29-h1-design-review.md.

shoulder_lift.source: shell v1: upper link meets the column at -100deg

elbow_flex.source: shell v1: wrist/gripper meet the base drum from +80deg with the shoulder at 0; 70deg keeps a 10deg margin

pairs.source: shell v1 shoulder x elbow sweep (15deg grid, pan 0, wrist 0): every colliding pose had shoulder_lift + elbow_flex >= 100deg (forearm/gripper fold into the base drum); 90deg keeps a 10deg margin. Wrist and pan variations not swept.

soft_limits.tcp_max_radius_source: horizontal distance from the shoulder_pan axis to the TCP (arm_spec.tcp_radius_m). Far reach dropped (user 2026-10-29); the zero pose sits at ~0.35 m and top-down picks within ~0.31 m; stretched out at ~0.44 m the shoulder needs ~9.4 kg.cm of the STS3215's rated 10 (estimate, docs/research/hardware-notes/2026-10-29-h1-design-review.md)
soft_limits.tcp_min_radius_source: motion test and workspace sweep 2026-10-31: tool straight down, open fingers hit the column at r <= 110 mm; folded with the tool tilted they hit it at r 130-135 mm. See docs/research/hardware-notes/2026-10-31-motion-test-results.md

floor.note: The arm must stay above the table and the base. Workspace sweep 2026-10-31: 1232 of 5460 poses that the other limits allowed overlapped them. Radii are the shell parts rounded up; a tool disc lies across the tool, so it adds nothing when the tool points straight down

tcp.name: finger_pad_center
tcp.source: shell v1: pad centre on the wrist_roll axis at the 40 mm holding width. It moves with the opening: use arm_spec.tcp_xyz_for_opening. Replaces the SO-101 URDF point, 7.9 mm off the roll axis

link_mass_note: Estimates from cad/shell_v1: printed part volume x 1.24 g/cm3 x 0.45 (not sliced or weighed), STS3215 55 g, STS3032 20 g, horn 4 g, 6806 bearing 22 g (assumed), lazy susan 70 g. gripper_link includes the fingers and links. No boards, wires or screws

gripper_kinematics.source: computed from cad/shell_v1/wrist_gripper_v1.py at each opening, not measured; fingertip_mm is along the tool from the wrist_roll joint
